newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 19.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:

WASHINGTON - An American lobbyist for the government of Pakistan complained to his client last summer that he had been "shaken down" for campaign contributions by Rep. Dan Burton (R-Ind.) who now is heading a House probe of alleged Democratic campaign fund-raising abuses.
INDIANAPOLIS - To his friends, Rep. Dan Burton, the Indiana Republican now running the House probe of political fund-raising, is an extraordinarily tenacious man.

WASHINGTON - Anthony Lake's nomination to head the CIA fell victim to "a cycle of political destruction" President Clinton complained, even as he pledged to announce "quite soon" a new candidate to lead the intelligence agency.
WASHINGTON - House Speaker Newt Gingrich's surprising decision to put off action temporarily on the Republicans' tax cut plan has infuriated dozens of fellow conservatives.

WASHINGTON - The new Washington, D.C., school administration proposed closing 16 of the city's 157 aging public schools, an unprecedented reduction that would be a major first step in the overhaul of the troubled system.
WASHINGTON - District of Columbia officials have discovered caches of stolen, decapitated parking meters at several sites across the city and they suspect it is the work of organized crime rings.
WASHINGTON - Seven times in the past eight weeks some residents of Montgomery County's most expensive neighborhoods have awakened in the wee hours to find armed men in their homes.
HO CHI MINH CITY, Vietnam - In an invasion of Vietnam 90s style, U.S. college graduates flock to the land that bitterly divided their parents' generation.
